Procedure

1Confirm stock, destination, and expected order type

Result
Stock is known and the expected transfer configuration is recorded.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 whwmd4300m000

Why LN works this way. Nothing yet. Reading inventory does not change with the transaction type, only what happens to the order does, and a transfer is proved at both ends, so both starting figures are needed. The expected order type comes from the origin and transaction-type combination in Default Order Types by Origin, and its warehousing procedure is what will decide which later steps LN runs itself.

StepActionYou should see
1.1Type the item in the filter box above the grid's Item column and press EnterThe item's row, and a row for any item whose code starts with it
1.2Tick the item's own rowThe header's links light up
1.3In the Inventory group, click Warehouse InventoryWarehouse - Item Inventory whwmd2515m000 opens, item carried throughWrite downitemsource warehousesource on-hand before
1.4In the same grid, find the row for the intended destination warehouseWrite downdestination warehousedestination on-hand before
1.5Open Warehousing➔Master Data➔Order Procedures➔Default Order Types by Origin (whinh0120m000)The default-order-type table opens
1.6With the toolbar's next-record and previous-record arrows, step until Order Origin reads Transfer (Manual), then find the row with transaction type Transfer, ship-from Warehouse, and ship-to WarehouseWrite downexpected warehousing order type;Create Shipment. For different source and destination warehouses, official help states Create Shipment = Always

2Create the transfer order

Result
A warehousing order exists with transaction type Transfer
Screen
Warehousing➔Orders➔Orders whinh2100m000

Why LN works this way. A manually created warehousing order has no originating package, so the transaction type is set by hand and the order number comes from the Warehousing number group rather than from a sales or purchase order. For a same-company transfer LN copies the outbound and shipment activities and then the inbound and inspection activities onto this one order, so it carries both sides of the move.

StepActionYou should see
2.1Open Warehousing➔Orders➔OrdersWarehousing Orders whinh2100m000 opens
2.2Click NewA blank warehousing-order header opens
2.3Set Order origin to Transfer (Manual)This is one of the ten manual order origins listed in the session help — section step 4.1
2.4Set Inventory Transaction Type to TransferOnly settable by hand because the order has no originating package — section step 4.1
2.5Set Ship-From Code to the source warehouse. It is the one from step 1.3
2.6Set Ship-To Code to the destination warehouse. It is the one from step 1.4Both types read Warehouse — the condition for the Transfer transaction type
2.7Compare the defaulted Warehousing Order Type with the one you expected. You recorded it at step 1.6
2.8Record the value actually usedWrite downactual warehousing order type
2.9Save the headerWrite downtransfer order number
2.10Add an order line with the item. It is the item from step 1.3
2.11Enter the quantity to moveWrite downtransferred quantity
2.12Save the line

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
No order number appearsHeader not saved, or a required field is still blank — recheck steps 2.3–2.8

3Confirm the processing path and create advice

Result
Manual and automatic activities are known before processing continues.
Screen
Warehousing➔Orders➔Outbound Line Status Overview whinh2129m000

Why LN works this way. The order type supplied a default procedure, and the header or the line may have overridden it. The activity table on the line is the only thing that says which steps LN will run automatically and which are yours, so it is read before advice is generated; predicting it from the item is how a step gets repeated or missed.

StepActionYou should see
3.1Open Outbound Line Status Overview whinh2129m000The outbound-line overview opens
3.2Find the transfer order line from Create the transfer orderThe item and order line match; Order Type matches the actual value from step 2.7
3.3Read every row in the Activities table, especially Finished and AutomaticAutomatic = Yes means LN runs it; Automatic = No means it is an operator step
3.4Record the activities marked Automatic = NoWrite downmanual outbound activities; these determine which later steps you perform
3.5If the next activity is automatic, choose Process on the warehousing orderLN executes consecutive automatic activities and stops at the next manual activity
3.6If Generate Outbound Advice is manual, open Outbound Lines and select the line
3.7Then choose Actions➔Advice➔Generate AdviceAdvised fills; automatic follow-on activities may also finish
3.8If Release Outbound Advice is manual and Released is still blank, choose Actions➔Advice➔Release AdviceReleased fills

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
Advice greyed outYou are on the session toolbar, not the Outbound Lines toolbar — see step 3.6

4Pick the goods

Result
Stock physically moves to staging at the source.
Screen
Warehousing➔Outbound/Inspections➔Picking List whinh4525m100

Why LN works this way. Picking is an activity only for a location-controlled warehouse, and a manual step only where the procedure says so; otherwise Picked fills without confirmation. The mechanics are the same session and actions as a sales pick, on the transfer's own outbound line.

StepActionYou should see
4.1Check the Picking List row recorded in Confirm the processing path and create adviceIf absent or already finished automatically, record Automatic / not applicable and skip steps 4.2–4.5; if Automatic = No, continue
4.2Find the Run for this orderThe line for your item and source warehouse
4.3Tick the line
4.4Actions➔Pick RunStock moves from the source location to staging. Picked fills on Outbound Lines
4.5Record the Run number from the headerWrite downpicking list Run number

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
No Run appears on the Picking ListIf the order already advanced, record Automatic / not observed. Otherwise, picking may not apply or advice was not generated; return to Confirm the processing path and create advice

5Ship

Result
Goods leave the source warehouse.
Screen
Warehousing➔Shipments➔Shipments whinh4130m000

Why LN works this way. A transfer between two different warehouses always creates a shipment; only a transfer within one warehouse does not. Whether that shipment is frozen and confirmed by you or by the procedure is the question Confirm the processing path and create advice's activity table answers.

StepActionYou should see
5.1Check the Freeze/Confirm Shipments/Loads row. You recorded it in Confirm the processing path and create adviceIf already finished automatically, record Automatic / not observed and skip steps 5.2–5.4; if Automatic = No, continue
5.2Find the shipment for this order, then click Drill InWrite downshipment number
5.3If Freeze Mandatory is ticked, choose Actions➔FreezeStatus = Frozen
5.4Choose Actions➔ConfirmStatus = Confirmed. Inventory leaves the source warehouse

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
No shipment is visible for a different-warehouse transferOfficial help says Create Shipment is Always. Check Shipment Lines and the Confirm the processing path and create advice activity status before continuing
Confirm greyed outShipment not yet Frozen, or Freeze Mandatory requires it — run step 5.3 first

6Receive at the destination

Result
Goods are put away in the destination warehouse.

Why LN works this way. The same order now runs its inbound half: the mandatory activities for any inbound line are the receipt and the inbound advice, and the transfer order's inbound lines are received and confirmed in the same receipt session a purchase uses. Confirming is what puts the goods away at the destination.

StepActionYou should see
6.1Open the Inbound Lines tab on the transfer orderThe inbound side of the same order, ship-to = destination warehouse
6.2Select the inbound line and choose Actions➔ReceiptWarehouse Receipt whinh3512m000 opens for the transfer line
6.3Select the receipt line and choose Actions➔ConfirmThe receipt is confirmed and the destination inventory is updated

7Verify it worked

Result
Source on-hand down, destination on-hand up, by the same quantity.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 whwmd4300m000

Why LN works this way. Nothing new. A transfer is proved twice: the source down and the destination up by the same quantity. A run can satisfy one half and not the other, which is why this task reads both.

StepActionYou should see
7.1Read on-hand for the item at both warehousesWrite downsource on-hand afterdestination on-hand after

Source on-hand before minus source on-hand after must equal the transferred quantity, and destination on-hand after minus destination on-hand before must equal the same figure. Warehouse transfer is complete only when both hold.

Warning
No recorded run has passed this proof yet. Read both warehouses' rows in one view at Confirm stock, destination, and expected order type, immediately before the transfer, and read them again here in the same view.

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
Destination on-hand did not riseThe receipt in Receive at the destination was not confirmed — return to the inbound line and Warehouse Receipt
Source and destination changes do not both equal the transfer quantityDo not approve the run. Recheck the Confirm stock, destination, and expected order type values and investigate unrelated inventory activity

Variations

CaseWhat changesTask
Multicompany warehouse transfer — source and destination warehouses in different logistic companiesLN generates two warehousing orders instead of one: the ship-from company's order carries the outbound and shipment activities, the ship-to company's carries inbound and inspection. Ship-to Code becomes meaningful. This changes the tasks (an order handoff is needed) and earns its own process rather than a row here
Planned/automated transfer, driven by Order PlanningTransfer Order Planning cppat1210m000, reached via Planning➔Plan Transfer➔Transfer Order Planning, generates transfer orders from planned inventory transactions rather than a person entering one by hand. Out of scope for this process.
Serialized or lot-controlled itemThe order header's Reclassification tab applies to rental and serialized transfers specifically. This variant is outside the scope of this process
